title: Bifunctional transition metal catalysts for high-current-density water electrolysis: mechanisms, strategies, and challenges
content: Non-noble transition-metal (TM) catalysts are promising for green H2 production because of their comparatively low cost and tunable electronic structures. However, many reported materials have been evaluated mainly at low current densities and for only one half-reaction. This review examines bifunctional catalysts for water electrolysis, using a geometric current-density magnitude of ≥500 mA cm−2 as the working definition of high-current-density operation. Low-current studies are retained to explain material-design principles and are distinguished from direct high-current validation. This review systematically addresses bifunctional TM catalysts for high current densities (≥500 mA cm−2). We outline the fundamental OER/HER mechanisms, define key performance metrics, and discuss catalyst and electrode structure designs. Key challenges and development pathways are critically examined. Finally, we present an integrated framework that coordinates catalyst, electrode, and system architecture, shifting the research paradigm from purely intrinsic activity towards system-level stability and efficiency. This perspective aims to accelerate the translation of laboratory discoveries into practical, durable water electrolysis technologies.
